A.explanation: About $140 \text{ N}$ results from using $3.5 \text{ m} \times \sin 35^\circ$ incorrectly or mishandling the moment balance.

B.explanation: About $170 \text{ N}$ comes from using the full $4.0 \text{ m}$ length for the cable position instead of $3.5 \text{ m}$ from the hinge.

C.explanation: Moments about the hinge give $T \sin 35^\circ \times 3.5 = 200 \times 2.0$, so $T$ is about $200 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: About $400 \text{ N}$ ignores the $\sin 35^\circ$ factor and balances $T$ directly against the $200 \text{ N}$ weight moment.

hints: Notice the hinge is the pivot: the $200 \text{ N}$ weight acts at the centre, $2.0 \text{ m}$ from the wall, while the cable pulls $0.50 \text{ m}$ from the far end, so $3.5 \text{ m}$ from the wall.
Only the vertical part of the cable pull can turn the horizontal bar about the hinge, so replace $T$ by $T \sin 35^\circ$ for the anticlockwise moment.
Set clockwise moment equal to anticlockwise moment: $200 \times 2.0 = T \sin 35^\circ \times 3.5$ and solve for $T$.
walkthrough: Take moments about the hinge at the wall so the unknown hinge forces have zero moment and can be ignored.
The uniform $200 \text{ N}$ bar acts at its centre, $2.0 \text{ m}$ from the hinge, giving clockwise moment $200 \times 2.0 = 400 \text{ N m}$.
The cable is attached $4.0 - 0.50 = 3.5 \text{ m}$ from the hinge at $35^\circ$ to the bar, so its perpendicular lever arm uses the vertical component $T \sin 35^\circ$.
For equilibrium, sum of moments is zero: $T \sin 35^\circ \times 3.5 - 200 \times 2.0 = 0$.
Substitute $\sin 35^\circ \approx 0.574$: $T = 400 / (3.5 \times 0.574) \approx 400 / 2.01 \approx 199 \text{ N}$, about $200 \text{ N}$ with unit $\text{N}$ as expected.
